LESSON: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you identify the setting -time and place-of a short story? 2. Why should one identify the different settings from which a story is based on?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy as learners manipulates digital devices with assistive technology to interact with different places at different

times.

● Imagination and creativity as learners apply creativity and imagination when teasing out the geographical setting, the historical

period and the culture from the short story.

Values:
● Unity: A learner enhances this value while working in groups and in pairs where the learners contribute to compare the

setting and places in the short story to their own real life setting,

● Respect: A learner enhances this as they value each other’s’ contributions during group work as they compare the setting

and places in the short story to their own real life setting,

Link to other subjects:

Comparing the setting and places in the short story is linked to reading short stories about settings in Kiswahili, Indigenous

languages and Creative Arts

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Audio-visual recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology
